latest.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Financial Foundation Models: A Survey
latest.summary: Financial foundation models increasingly support workflows spanning financial question answering, disclosure analysis, forecasting, and decision-making. In these settings, uncertainty may concern whether evidence is valid and available at the relevant time, whether an interpretation is justified, which outcomes remain plausible, or which action is preferred under costs and risk constraints. Because these objects arise at different points in a workflow, uncertainty cannot be reduced to confidence in a final output. We introduce a source-aware framework that distinguishes six sources of uncertainty across evidence and context, model and inference, and outcome and action, while treating…

latest.summary: Abstract Cerebral cortical development is a finely regulated process, depending on key neuronal progenitors, giving rise to post-mitotic neurons that migrate to superficial regions in the developing brain. Disruptions can give rise to severe cortical malformations that are associated with intellectual disability and intractable epilepsy. In developing mutant mouse brains, ectopic apical radial glia (aRG) progenitors were found outside the normal proliferative ventricular zone (VZ). latest.title: GNN-Enhanced TCN Algorithms for ECG Anomaly Detection
latest.summary: To a time series can be also given the structure of directed graph, opening the doors to the usage of graph neural networks (GNNs) in this context. In this paper we develop a new pipeline involving novel geometric deep learning models that merge the capabilities of ordinary TCNs with the ones of GNNs to solve an anomaly detection problem on electrocardiogram signals.

We characterize the spectral density from which RHFF frequencies are drawn, allowing kernels such as the Matérn family to be specified directly in the frequency domain. items.title: RobPiCFM: A Training-Free Target-Conditioned Method with Foundation Models for Robotic Picking in Clutter
items.summary: Picking objects from clutter remains a challenging problem in robotic manipulation, as it requires connecting object-level perception, grasp generation, collision-aware selection, and robot motion execution in unstructured scenes. In this paper, we present RobPiCFM, an open-source, trainingfree method for target-conditioned picking in cluttered scenes. The proposed method combines pretrained foundation-modelbased perception with RGB-D geometry, 6D object pose estimation and tracking, grasp candidate generation, constraintbased grasp filtering, and motion planning. Unlike end-toend manipulation policies, the method does not require taskspecific policy learning and relies instead on…

items.title: Adversarial Post-Training of Foundation Models for High-Frequency Trading
items.summary: While autoregressive foundation models trained on limit order book (LOB) data show state-of-the-art performance for market simulation, pre-training with cross-entropy neither penalizes the compounding of sampling errors over free-running rollouts nor targets desired market properties. We introduce a post-training method for LOB foundation models using a Wasserstein generative adversarial network (GAN) objective. A critic, trained online on rollouts through the true, non-differentiable matching engine, guides updates from evolution strategies over rank-4 LoRA perturbations of the pre-trained generator, under a KL trust region. items.title: SpaRRTa: A Synthetic Benchmark for Evaluating Spatial Intelligence in Visual Foundation Models
items.summary: Abstract Visual Foundation Models (VFMs), such as DINO and CLIP, excel in semantic understanding of images but exhibit limited spatial reasoning capabilities, which limits their applicability to embodied systems. As a result, recent work has incorporated some 3D tasks (such as depth estimation) into VFM training. However, VFM performance remains inconsistent across other spatial tasks, raising the question of whether these models truly possess spatial awareness or overfit to specific 3D objectives. To address this question, we introduce the Spatial Relation Recognition Task (SpaRRTa) benchmark, which evaluates the ability of VFMs to identify static directional relations between visible…

items.title: UVM: neuron verification
items.summary: The significant growth in Neuromorphic engineering in the last few years has generated a multitude of biologically plausible neuron models that have been developed into Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) and Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) designs. These neuron models range in complexity, from the Integrate and Fire model to the Hodgkin-Huxley model. When creating fixed point implementations of these models, it is prudent to ensure the dynamic range of the fixed point conversion has been correctly chosen. However, verifying neuron model implementations in simulation requires a significant amount of time to achieve an acceptable coverage; that is, everything that could be…

items.title: Learning the spikes
items.summary: Existing AI methods consume vast amounts of power due to their large scale and intrinsic redundancy. Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer a biologically plausible alternative that enables systems that are of a low Size, Weight and Power (SWaP) profile, once implemented. However, there is limited commercial availability of Neuromorphic processors to efficiently implement these SNNs on chip, resulting in a requirement to develop FPGA-based Neuromorphic processing. The same can be said for Neuromorphic sensors, driving a trend to develop techniques for encoding existing sensor data into an event-based format for use with Neuromorphic processors. This paper presents a very efficient, low power…

items.title: Modelling dynamic systems transfer functions from events in computational neuromorphic imaging
items.summary: Event Vision Sensing (EVS) report threshold crossings of log-irradiance, so a static optical system imaging a static scene produces no output at all. The classical procedure for measuring a Point Spread Function (PSF), illuminating the system with a constant point source, therefore has no event-based equivalent: the probe must carry a temporal profile, and that profile becomes part of the measurement. items.summary: This paper investigates non-thermal electromagnetic radiation generated within livingorganisms. In addition to universal blackbody radiation dominating the infrared spectrum,living systems generate narrow-band, coherent infrared radiation aligned with the 8–13 µmtransparency window of Earth’s atmosphere. This emission avoids complete thermalization,acts independently of classical thermal radiance, and represents an evolutionary hallmarkof biological order. The radiation is shown to originate within multi-connected networks ofsuperconducting microtubules functioning as Josephson junctions during action potentialpropagation. items.title: In silico drug discovery framework leveraging biomedical foundation models and evaluating generative models-a use case on 3CL pro .
items.summary: AI models such as foundation models and generative models have shown promise for aiding drug discovery alongside traditional cheminformatics and bioinformatics tools and physics-based approaches. In this study, we design a workflow that integrates these AI methods to generate molecules alongside established informatic and predictive filtering approaches to streamline downselection of molecules from the massive and noisy result sets generated by AI. This workflow evaluates generative methods based on validity, reliability, diversity, similarity, hallucination and campaign needs. Analyses are made on the original proprietary dataset to determine molecular property thresholds for screening…

items.title: MicroDUET: a dual-headed genomic foundation model for pathogen surveillance
items.summary: Pathogen genomic surveillance works from raw reads, assembled genomes and alignments, representations that are slow and costly to compare at scale. Compact embeddings from genomic language models offer an alternative, but surveillance requires resolving both evolutionary ancestry (phylogeny) and phenotypic capability (function) - which need not co-vary. Here we present MicroDUET, which adapts a 26.6-million-parameter ProkBERT backbone with two 3.5-million-parameter adapter heads: a phylogeny head trained contrastively on genome windows from the same microbes, and a function head trained to identify genes across taxa. On held-out retrieval benchmarks, the phylogeny head returned the correct…

items.title: Systematic benchmarking of molecular foundation models for natural-product annotation and biosynthetic inference
items.summary: Abstract Molecular foundation models offer a potential route to improve natural-product annotation and support biosynthetic inference, but their utility across these tasks remains insufficiently characterized. We benchmarked eight foundation-model representations against Morgan fingerprints across five tasks covering natural-product-likeness, natural product chemical class prediction, PMN and KEGG pathway association, and PlantCyc reaction-neighbor prediction. Models were evaluated under random and scaffold-based splits using both full data and sample-efficiency settings. In the full data setting, MolFormer achieved the highest mean AUROC for natural product likeness prediction, while…

items.title: LUNA-FM: a subword foundation model for long non-coding RNAs for functional inference.
items.summary: RNA foundation models (FMs) have shown promise for RNA identification and functional annotation. However, many use single-nucleotide tokenization, which produces long input sequences and can increase computational costs when modelling long RNAs, including long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs). To address these limitations, we introduce LUNA-FM ( Length-efficient s U bword-based N ucleic A cid F oundation M odel) , an RNA language model pretrained on approximately 28 million redundancy-filtered ncRNA sequences. LUNA-FM combines subword tokenization with a long context transformer, enabling efficient modelling of long RNA transcripts. We systematically evaluate tokenization strategies and…

items.title: Toward precision nanomedicine via artificial intelligence guided design and prediction.
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing nanomedicine development by linking formulation variables and biological context with delivery, therapeutic efficacy, and safety. This review examines AI assisted formulation design, centralized formulation databases, prediction of nanoparticle self assembly, and models of cell and tissue selective delivery, biodistribution, and therapeutic outcomes. Recent advances in predicting nanotoxicity and nanoparticle induced immune responses further emphasize the importance of incorporating safety endpoints into nanomedicine optimization. Beyond nanocarrier engineering, foundation models and multimodal analyses of single-cell and spatial data are expanding…

items.title: Fluid eMTBR-tau243 as a Biomarker of Mixed 3-Repeat and 4-Repeat Tau Pathology.
items.summary: Neurodegenerative diseases with abnormal tau protein aggregation in the brain (ie, tauopathies) can be classified by the tau isoform that accumulates: 3-repeat (3R), 4-repeat (4R), or mixed 3R/4R tauopathies, which include chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), some forms of frontotemporal lobar degeneration, and Alzheimer disease (AD). The endogenously cleaved form of tau microtubule binding region containing the residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) can be detected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and blood and has been associated with AD tau pathology, but its specificity and biological interpretation in non-AD tauopathies remains unclear. To evaluate biofluid eMTBR-tau243 in a range of tauopathies.…

items.title: HDAC6 Inhibition Promotes Peripheral Nerve Development and Regeneration via Neurofilament Acetylation.
items.summary: Peripheral nerve injury remains challenging due to limited neuronal regeneration. Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) regulates microtubule dynamics, but its role in peripheral nervous system (PNS) development and repair is incompletely understood. This study investigates the expression, function, and mechanism of HDAC6 in PNS maturation and regeneration. HDAC6 was abundantly expressed in dorsal root ganglia and sciatic nerves. During postnatal development (P1-P28), HDAC6 expression progressively declined, inversely correlating with increased α-tubulin K40 and global acetylation. items.title: NiCl 2 affect N- and O -alkylations during alkaloid biosynthesis in Penicillium oxalicum .
items.summary: Oxaline is one fungal alkaloid possessing important citotoxicity and inhibiting tubulin polymerisation. The alkaloids in this series are differentiated by the degree of alkylation promoted by SAM-dependent methyl transferases, being oxaline the end product in the biosynthetic cascade. During our studies, it was found that the addition of NiCl2 into liquid culture of P. oxalicum affect the distribution of these alkaloids, lowering the production of oxaline and enhancing the amount of methylglandicoline A and glandicoline C, two unreported natural products. Ni(II) addition also resulted in the production of a pair of E/Z isomers of N-formyl α,β-dehydro-DOPA, found only at trace amounts in…

items.title: Dual-Mode MoS 2 /PdSe 2 /WS 2 Van Der Waals Heterostructure for Self-Powered Polarization Sensing and Neuromorphic Processing.
items.summary: Harsh maritime environments demand compact visual devices capable of self-powered photodetection, polarization sensing, and motion-trajectory extraction for onboard processing. Here, we demonstrate a bias-switchable MoS2/PdSe2/WS2 van der Waals heterostructure (vdWH) that integrates self-powered polarization-sensitive photodetection and optoelectronic synaptic functionality. At a drain-source voltage (Vds) of 0 V, built-in electric fields efficiently separate photogenerated carriers, enabling self-powered broadband detection over the 405-658 nm spectral range. The device exhibits a maximum responsivity of 1345 mA W-1, a specific detectivity of 8.89 × 1010 Jones, and rapid rise/fall times…

items.title: Ion-Access Engineering for High-Performance Vertical Organic Electrolyte-Gated Transistors.
items.summary: Organic electrolyte-gated transistors (OEGTs) are promising platforms for bioelectronics and neuromorphic systems owing to their low-voltage operation and strong ionic-electronic coupling. However, in vertical OEGTs, which offer higher current densities and faster switching, the semiconductor channel is often shielded from direct electrolyte contact, limiting ionic accessibility and resulting in inefficient gate coupling and slow switching dynamics. Here, we introduce a photolithography-free ion-access strategy for vertical OEGTs, combining femtosecond laser micropatterning with inkjet-printed solid-state electrolytes. items.title: Molecularly Programmed Stress Dissipation Strategy for Ultrastretchable Neuromorphic Electronics.
items.summary: Intrinsically stretchable organic synaptic transistors (ISOSTs) using semiconducting polymers (SPs) hold promise for on-body signal processing by mimicking biological synaptic functions and processing temporal bio-signals directly at or near the point of data acquisition. However, conventional SPs designed primarily to increase polymer softness and mechanical compliance often lack molecular-level mechanisms for effective stress dissipation, thereby limiting device-level stretchability to below 100% and causing substantial degradation in electrical performance. Here, we demonstrate ISOSTs achieving 150% device-level stretchability through molecularly programmed stress dissipation (MPSD) of…

items.title: Love numbers for the Myers-Perry geometry
items.summary: We analyze Love numbers for scalar fields in the Myers-Perry geometry in arbitrary dimensions. The tidal responses of black holes are specified by two constants which encode a potential logarithmic running and the Love number. We argue that the parameter specifying the running is not sensitive to the structure of the horizon, and we explicitly compute this parameter for Myers-Perry black holes in arbitrary dimensions by utilizing the asymptotic expansion of the wave equation. The Love numbers rely on the details of the boundary conditions at the horizon, and we compute them using several distinct approximations.

items.title: The lifting problem for Galois representations of global fields
items.summary: We prove that all mod $2$ Galois representations of a global field lift modulo $4$. In contrast, for every odd prime $p$, we exhibit examples of global Galois representations modulo $p$ that do not lift modulo $p^2$. Our methods also allow us to prove liftability of generalized quaternion groups and hence to complete the classification of liftable finite groups initiated by Khare and Merkurjev.

items.title: Inter-Nanoparticle Repulsion Effect on Self-Organization in Polymer Nanocomposites: A Langevin Dynamics Simulation Study
items.summary: Demixing through liquid-liquid phase separation is relevant to nanoparticle (NP) aggregation in polymer nanocomposites (PNCs), biomolecular compartmentalization, and liquids embedded in elastic networks. Mixing-demixing phase behavior depends on factors, such as particle size distribution, system dimen-sionality, intermolecular interactions, and relative concentrations. Here, using Langevin Dynamics simu-lations, we systematically investigate the effect of inter-nanoparticle repulsion on the self-assembly of PNCs under extreme confinement. A nanoparticle assembly, in the form of a compact droplet, is immersed in a polymer matrix of semiflexible, rod-like chains. By varying the…

items.title: SpotDiff: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Zero-Shot Change Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
items.summary: Remote sensing change detection usually relies on large collections of temporally aligned, pixel-level annotations, which limits its scalability across regions, imaging platforms and application domains. Recent zero-shot approaches reduce the need for supervision, but they often localize fine-grained changes poorly because their features are coarse or inconsistent across time. We present SpotDiff, a training-free, plug-and-play framework for zero-shot change detection built by composing complementary vision foundation models. SpotDiff uses DINOv3 for semantically robust features, AnyUp to reconstruct them at pixel resolution, and SAM 3 for text-guided region-of-interest proposals, which an…

items.title: AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics
items.summary: Neural surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD) are trained and ranked on datasets that each vary one design family in one flow domain. Such datasets cannot test the least that an aerodynamic foundation model must do: predict CFD-quality incompressible flow in seconds for new shapes in new enclosures. On DrivAerML, larger models and longer training barely lower Transolver's error; doubling the training cases cuts it by about 12% up to 400 cases, exhausting the dataset. We introduce AeroZoo, a benchmark and training corpus of 3,815 time-mean solutions to the unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) equations with a transition model, across seven geometry families, eight…

items.title: HiVE-VQA: Hierarchical Interaction via Volumetric Embedding for Video Quality Assessment
items.summary: The proliferation of user-generated video content has made accurate and robust no-reference video quality assessment (NR-VQA) a highly important challenge. Existing research increasingly relies on architecturally complex multi-branch pipelines or computationally intensive fine-tuning of single-branch backbones. In this paper, we investigate whether a single frozen video foundation model can serve as an effective NR-VQA backbone, and propose HiVE-VQA, the first framework (to our knowledge) to apply a JEPA-based video encoder to this task. HiVE-VQA extracts token grids from multiple depths of a pre-trained V-JEPA 2.1 encoder and stacks them into a hierarchical spatio-temporal volume, which a…

items.title: Library of peptides: Analysis of a complex reactive mixture with the use of statistical physics and inference
items.summary: Self-assembled mixtures enable the exploration of vast chemical diversity, yet characterizing the hundreds of coexisting species they contain remains a major challenge. Standard analytical techniques such as chromatography and spectroscopy produce overlapping signals that cannot be resolved by conventional deconvolution methods, which neglect the concentration correlations imposed by the reactive network. Here, we introduce a framework that bridges statistical physics and analytical chemistry to deconvolute complex self-assembled mixtures from partial spectral data. Inspired by Potts models of protein folding, we express the chemical potential of each compound as a function of a reduced…

items.title: Acoustically driven motion of single molecules at hBN surfaces
items.summary: Developments in single-molecule imaging and sensing techniques have enabled direct observation of biomolecular dynamics at interfaces, which has important implications for the fields of membrane biophysics, nanofluidic sensing and transport. However, integrating active surface transport, localization and control over molecule motion remains challenging, limiting further progress in the realization of single-molecule devices. Here, we introduce an integrated surface acoustic wave (SAW)-hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) platform as a contactless actuation platform for directional transport of biomolecules over hBN surfaces. hBN provides an atomically flat surface on which DNA can be confined and…

items.title: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
items.summary: Embodied foundation models hinge on diverse robot interaction data, which are costly to collect. Egocentric human videos offer a complementary source of experience, and latent action models (LAMs) provide a popular means of leveraging these videos for policy supervision. Compared with world-action models (WAMs), LAMs can offer greater training efficiency and potentially lower inference costs by avoiding explicit pixel prediction during policy learning and execution. However, most existing LAMs learn latent actions solely through video reconstruction, which can cause their representations to cluster by visual appearance rather than by the underlying actions. As a result, they struggle to…

items.title: TuMAP: A Dual-View, Morphotype-Aware Pathomics Pipeline for Quantifying Renal Tubular Remodeling
items.summary: Quantifying disease-associated renal tubular remodeling is challenging because tubular appearances are heterogeneous. We introduce TuMAP (Tubular Morphotype-Aware Pathomics), a pipeline combining (1) dual-view foundation-model representations and provisional morphotype annotation, (2) compositional and within-morphotype pathomics, and (3) patient-level statistical inference. From 456,158 tubules in 358 PAS-stained kidney biopsy slides, TuMAP identified eight image-based morphotypes, seven of which showed stable subsampling assignments. Across 219 patients in six diagnostic groups, diabetic nephropathy (DN) and tubulointerstitial nephritis/acute tubular injury (TIN/ATI) each differed from…

items.title: Reasoning Supervision and Capability Retention in LoRA Domain Adaptation
items.summary: Fine-tuning foundation models on financial data has a wide range of applications, including identifying event types from news, monitoring risk and compliance language, and answering questions over filings and earnings calls. In this setting, the main challenge is to improve task performance without degrading the generalization capabilities of the model. In this paper, we present an extensive set of ablations for fine-tuning Qwen3-8B with low-rank adaptation (LoRA). We compare three training regimes: (1) response-only LoRA, where the supervised response is the label alone; (2) single-adapter reasoning, where reasoning traces from a teacher model are included alongside the labels in the…

items.title: Ropedia Xperience 2: A Gold Standard for Scaling Physical AI Environments and Behaviors
items.summary: Large foundation models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 have recently been shown to control robots directly from visual observations. They nevertheless remain brittle on long-horizon, contact-rich tasks in real-world environments. Further progress depends on two complementary resources: demonstrations of human behavior that supervise how tasks are performed, and interactive environments in which policies can be rolled out, evaluated, and improved in closed loop. Language models have advanced along well-characterized scaling laws; the corresponding question for physical AI is how capability scales with environments and behaviors, which first requires identifying which data to scale…

items.title: De Sitter Gravity and Emergent Time from Fusion Matrix Product States and SYK
items.summary: We propose a quantum-mechanical model dual to two-dimensional de Sitter (dS) gravity. It is a quantum channel, defined by a matrix product state that fuses one spin at each step, and is related to a limit of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model without chord crossings. Its simplest part is a random walk with an emergent $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ symmetry, which we identify with the symmetry of the future boundary of dS. It selects a time variable in which the walk obeys the Schwarzian action and yields the disk amplitude of dS Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity. As the simplest case, we consider free massless scalar fields in the fixed background of dS$_2$. We find the agreement of the two-point function in the…

items.title: Your Vision Foundation Model Is Secretly an EEG Foundation Model
items.summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models are pretrained on thousands of hours of recordings, yet their frozen features transfer poorly to downstream tasks, and this transfer does not consistently improve with larger models or more pretraining data. We show that a vision foundation model that has never seen EEG is a stronger frozen EEG encoder than these specialized models, once the signals are rendered as images that a vision transformer can read. Our method, SeeEEG, keeps the vision backbone frozen and learns only how EEG is displayed to it. Each channel occupies a dedicated row of patches and is drawn either as a waveform at a fixed gain or as a scalogram whose frequency range…

items.title: Spin to win: enhancing the quantum Otto cycle with the circular Unruh effect
items.summary: We study a quantum Otto cycle whose working medium is a qubit Unruh-DeWitt detector undergoing uniform circular motion in $(3+1)$-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, interacting with a massless scalar field in a thermal state during the isochoric strokes. We compute the detector's transition rate and determine its energy gap-dependent effective temperature, showing that the effective temperature can be higher than the ambient bath temperature in the small energy gap limit and lower in the high bath temperature limit. We then investigate how these motion-induced effective temperatures affect the operating conditions and performance of the quantum Otto cycle as a heat engine or a refrigerator.…

items.title: AI for Biologists: The Knowledge Boundaries of Foundation Models in the Age of Agentic Systems
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how biological research is done. Biological foundation models trained on millions of nucleotides, protein, and single-cell measurements predict protein structures, mutation effects, and cellular responses to genetic perturbations. Agentic systems, AI assistants built on large language models, can run multistep analyses from plain-language requests and increasingly call foundation models as tools. Yet it is often unclear when these models' outputs can be trusted. We frame this as a model's knowledge boundary: the range of inputs, tasks, and conditions over which its outputs are reliable. This review explains how foundation models are built and…

items.title: Compiling Known Rules into Compact Neural Agents: Weight-Space Programming on Unseen Games
items.summary: Weight-space programming (WSP) uses language models to construct neural network weights without training. We test whether known game mechanics can be compiled into compact agents that generalise to held-out levels, renderings and start states within a game family. Writers receive simulator source with held-out level data removed for 20 privately authored, unpublished ARC-AGI-3-style game families. With a fixed 57k-parameter recurrent architecture, the strongest writer reaches 56% held-out-level success with feedback, while the four main writers' Python players reach 97-100%. An exploratory free-architecture condition reaches 68-90%. Learning from support-level examples transfers much less…

items.title: Universal Infectious Disease Forecasting with Mantis 2
items.summary: Public health agencies need to anticipate how outbreaks will unfold, when they will peak, and how long demand on health services will remain elevated. We previously developed a foundation model, Mantis, which was trained entirely on simulated outbreaks---enabling us to generate the diversity and scale of training data needed to support forecasting across diseases. However, our previous work left unresolved when simulation improves predictions and how it should complement observational data. Here, we varied the balance of simulated and observed training data while holding forecasting tasks fixed and varying the available surveillance history. We found that simulation-rich training was…

items.title: Time Flies When You Parallelise: Pareto-efficient Time Series Foundation Models with Linear Recurrences
items.summary: Time series foundation models have demonstrated strong zero-shot forecasting performance, but computational efficiency remains a central architectural challenge. Temporal self-attention incurs quadratic cost in the number of temporal tokens, while nonlinear recurrent state transitions restrict parallel computation along the temporal dimension. We introduce ci-proto, a family of time series foundation models based on Mamba-3, whose linear state recurrences support chunk-wise parallel-in-time computation during training, and inference costs that scale linearly with sequence length. The architecture alternates recurrent temporal processing with cross-variate attention, supporting multivariate…

items.title: Kosmo-GFM: A Production-Ready Geometry Foundation Model
items.summary: We present Kosmo-GFM, a scene reconstruction system that integrates a geometry foundation model (GFM), a pose optimization engine (PoseEngine), and reconstruction-derived supervision from KosmoWorld. GFM predicts camera parameters, depth, cross-view correspondences, and dynamic 3D points from images and videos. PoseEngine combines these predictions with geometric optimization to recover scene-level camera poses and geometry for downstream 3D and 4D Gaussian Splatting. KosmoWorld generates images and geometric supervision from reconstructed real-world scenes to improve GFM's geometric predictions. On the Sparse and Medium subsets of SpatialBench, GFM achieves the lowest absolute relative…

items.title: From Foundation VLM to Versatile Driving VLM: A Triplet Incremental Training Approach
items.summary: Adapting general Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to Autonomous Driving (AD) is thought to require heavy 3D spatial priors or intrusive architectural overhauls to compensate for a lack of spatial grounding. In this work, we present a counterintuitive pilot study: off-the-shelf general VLMs already exhibit remarkable adaptability across diverse driving tasks, while precise metric depth remains the primary missing link, a bottleneck readily addressable via onboard sensors and depth foundation models. To this end, we introduce the Triplet Incremental Training Framework, a non-intrusive paradigm that seamlessly instills 3D geometric awareness into a general VLM backbone while fully preserving its…

items.title: MusicRWKV: A Multimodal RWKV Framework for Music Representation Learning
items.summary: Recent music foundation models have achieved remarkable progress in music representation learning, yet most existing approaches rely on Transformer architectures whose quadratic attention complexity introduces substantial computational and memory overhead when modeling long-duration music recordings. In this work, we propose MusicRWKV, a multimodal music representation learning framework built upon the RWKV architecture. MusicRWKV jointly models waveform, spectrogram, and metadata information within a unified self-supervised learning framework. To improve efficiency for long musical sequences, we introduce an invertible compression module that reduces sequence length while preserving…

items.title: Directionally Supervised Neuromorphic Protection for Distribution Systems Using Local Measurements
items.summary: Reliable protection under varying power system operating conditions requires rapid fault detection while preserving selectivity against external faults and non-fault disturbances. This requirement is particularly challenging in communication-free schemes, where relays must determine trip conditions solely from local electrical measurements. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a directionally supervised neuromorphic protection scheme that integrates disturbance-responsive leaky integrate-and-fire dynamics with a direction-dependent firing threshold to distinguish internal faults from reverse-direction events. The unified relay architecture combines local disturbance detection,…

items.title: Transferable Neuromorphic Protection for Distribution Networks
items.summary: Protection of converter-dominated distribution networks is challenging due to limited fault currents, operating-mode transitions, bidirectional power flow, and heterogeneous network configurations. This paper proposes a scale-invariant neuromorphic protection framework to enable transferable protection decisions across such networks. The framework integrates asset-based normalization, multi-domain disturbance representation, event-driven spike encoding, leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) dynamics, adaptive threshold regulation, and directional supervision within a unified mathematical formulation. Local voltage, current, active power, and reactive power measurements are transformed into…

items.title: GNN-Enhanced TCN Algorithms for ECG Anomaly Detection
items.summary: To a time series can be also given the structure of directed graph, opening the doors to the usage of graph neural networks (GNNs) in this context. In this paper we develop a new pipeline involving novel geometric deep learning models that merge the capabilities of ordinary TCNs with the ones of GNNs to solve an anomaly detection problem on electrocardiogram signals.

items.title: STVLA: Spatial-aware and Temporal-memory forVision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Robotic manipulation often requires both spatial scene understanding and task history. However, many vision-language-action (VLA) policies rely primarily on current observations, without explicitly integrating spatial structure and task history. Appearance-based memories can be sensitive to occlusion and viewpoint changes, while spatial representations of the current scene alone do not preserve how the scene has changed during task execution. We introduce STVLA, a framework that incorporates features from a pretrained visual geometry foundation model into temporal memory alongside visual representations. This allows the policy to recall past scene structure as context for current action…

items.title: ReA-Bench: Benchmarking Responsible Agent Auditing
items.summary: As agents perform tasks autonomously in local and cloud environments, auditing their execution trajectories can help service providers identify risks and improve agent harnesses and foundation models. Our analysis of production and red-team trajectories shows that some risks are repeatedly missed across auditing configurations. Overall recall obscures which risks are missed and whether higher recall comes with more false positives on legitimate behavior. Existing benchmarks offer limited insight into these failures. Generated trajectories can contain inconsistent tool calls and responses, conspicuous risky actions, or repetitive attack patterns. Grouping results by risk type also makes it…

items.title: HeMeR: Heterogeneous Memory Reconciliation for Embodied Agents via Structured KV Reuse
items.summary: Embodied agents make decisions by combining information from heterogeneous memory modules, including declarative memory for explicit knowledge, procedural memory for learned routines, and working memory for current observations. During interaction, the memory contents required for decision making change with the agent's state, goal, and task progress, while many contents remain shared across consecutive decisions. However, existing memory modules are typically accessed through separate interfaces, so each updated memory context is often processed as a new input to the foundation model. This prevents selective key-value (KV) cache reuse for unchanged memory contents and forces full KV cache…

items.title: Helgason-Fourier Random Features for Scalable Hyperbolic Latent Variables
items.summary: Hyperbolic geometry is well suited to embedding hierarchical data, capturing tree-like structure faithfully even in the low dimensions where Euclidean dimensionality reduction is severely constrained. We introduce Random Helgason--Fourier Features (RHFF), an explicit finite-dimensional feature map for kernels on hyperbolic space. We characterize the spectral density from which RHFF frequencies are drawn, allowing kernels such as the Matérn family to be specified directly in the frequency domain. We also prove a uniform approximation error bound for RHFF. Building on this representation, we develop a hyperbolic latent variable model called RHFF-LVM, which requires no numerical quadrature,…

items.title: Rational Alignments of Superintelligences via Debates
items.summary: Artificial superintelligences (ASI) is artificial intelligences with greater capability. However, as human principal has to use it, we have to ensure that the agent will perform in the interest of the human. We investigate the framework of ASI-assisted question answering where ASI agents know the correct answer but the human does not. We provide some example of mechanism for rational alignment, where the agent utility is unchanged, but the interaction between the agent and the human principal is controlled to be in a certain fashion. We show specifically that a debate framework where the agents can further reason and behave in a subgame perfect equilibrium manner will lead to a more…

items.title: Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: It is common to train Large Language Models (LLMs) for agentic tasks with Reinforcement Learning (RL) from scalar rewards. However, this throws away the fine-grained information about the environment that the agent experienced during the trial (e.g., error logs). To utilize this rich information, recent works wrap the agent in a harness that refines its own inputs through reflection or compaction and hands past experience to future rollouts, but the construction of the handed-off artifacts (e.g., a playbook) is itself not learned. We want the best of both worlds: gradient updates from a scalar reward, while also utilizing environment information to hand off experience. As a concrete…

items.title: On Energy-Based Modelling for Fluidic Excitable Neurons
items.summary: Motivated by the potential of pneumatic excitable devices in soft robotics, this paper develops an energy-based, domain-agnostic equivalent of the Hodgkin-Huxley modelling framework using bond graph theory. The proposed model is used to guide the design of a pneumatic excitable neuron. The potential of this approach is illustrated through the design of a pneumatic half-center oscillator, an essential building block for rhythmic neuromorphic behaviours.

items.title: Responsible AI and Structural Justice
items.summary: This Element presents challenges of attributing responsibility for AI harms through political theories of structural injustice, where fault is broadly diffused and difficult to establish. I argue that AI systems feature complex structural entanglements between humans and machines-in computational architectures, organizational workflows, and societal data collectives-that pose problems for conventional liability where direct causal links are necessary for blame. I develop two modes of structural responsibility that address unjust AI outcomes from these entanglements. Thin structural responsibility traces where power and accountability lie in the processes of developing unjust AI systems.…

items.title: Hyperbolic Large Language Models
items.summary: Abstract. Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success and demonstrated superior performance across various tasks, including natural language processing (NLP), weather forecasting, biological protein folding, text generation, and solving mathematical problems. However, many real-world data exhibit highly non-Euclidean latent hierarchical anatomy, such as protein networks, transportation networks, financial networks, brain networks, and linguistic structures or syntactic trees in natural languages. Effectively learning intrinsic semantic entailment and hierarchical relationships from these raw, unstructured input data using LLMs remains an underexplored area. Due to its…

items.title: The Substrate Effect: Rice Husk Versus Cotton Gin Trash in Mycelium-Based Composite Production
items.summary: Mycelium-based composites (MBCs) are emerging as low-carbon materials for converting agricultural residues into construction-oriented panels. However, the specific role of substrate selection remains difficult to define because fungal species, nutrient systems, and processing conditions often vary between studies. Here, rice husk and cotton gin trash were directly compared as locally available Australian feedstocks for heat-pressed MBC panels under the same cultivation and fabrication framework. Four white-rot fungal isolates, Amauroderma sp., Ganoderma sp., Pycnoporus coccineus, and Trametes hirsuta, were cultivated with wheat grains as a nutrient supplement, enabling the substrate effect…

Digital Twin Development of Mycelium-based Engineered Living Materials

To bypass the strict environmental and regulatory constraints associated with physical cultivation, this chapter introduces a multi-stage framework designed to build a mycelium-based digital twin. items.title: Wear-Time Detection for Lower-Back Wearable Devices: A Validation Study from Signal Processing to Foundation Models
items.summary: Accurate wear-time detection is essential for valid digital mobility assessment, yet existing lower-back device algorithms rely on heuristic thresholds validated only against stationary non-wear time, with no study benchmarking these methods on a common dataset. We benchmarked the full spectrum of wear-time detection approaches for lower-back devices, from signal processing to foundation models, using three complementary datasets: real-world recordings from 14 younger adults with labelled wear/non-wear periods, 12 recordings of non-wear with artificial device movement, and the Mobilise-D Technical Validation Study (n=101, target clinical population, 100% wear). items.title: A dual locally active memristive Hopfield neural network: hidden dynamics and multistability for medical image encryption.
items.summary: The increasing demand for secure medical image transmission exposes limitations of conventional encryption. This work presents a two-memristor Hopfield neural network (2 M-HNN) incorporating two locally active memristors: a multi-equilibrium-state memristor with trigonometric-polynomial hybrid memductance and Gaussian-localized flux perturbation, emulating electromagnetic irradiation, and a Gaussian-envelope rational memristor with sech2 damping, replicating autaptic synaptic feedback. items.title: Monolithic Fabrication of Flexible Optoelectronic Neuromorphic Synapses with Bandgap-Engineered Centimeter-Scale SnSe2 van der Waals Layers.
items.summary: The transition of bandgap energies in two-dimensional (2D) materials driven by their miniaturization opens up opportunities for emerging device technologies unattainable with conventional approaches. Herein, "all" 2D optoelectronic synapse devices are reported employing the transition characteristics of wafer-scale 2D tin diselenide (SnSe2) layers directly grown on polymeric substrates at a low temperature of 300 °C. items.summary: Abstract Universities are adopting artificial intelligence through cloud platforms, enterprise assistants, learning systems, research tools, and administrative analytics, yet most institutions lack a method for judging whether these arrangements preserve meaningful digital autonomy. This methodological paper develops the University AI Sovereignty Index (UASI), a multidimensional assessment of an institution's practical capacity to choose, govern, scrutinise, and, when necessary, exit AI dependencies. items.title: Effect of xanthan gum on 3D-printed dysphagia foods.
items.summary: Background The global trend of population ageing is progressively worsening, leading to an increasing prevalence of dysphagia among the elderly population. Meanwhile, 3D printing technology offers a viable solution by providing customized, nutrient-rich, dysphagia-friendly foods for affected individuals. This study utilized Pleurotus ostreatus mycelium (POM), xanthan gum (XG), and egg white protein as primary materials. Building upon previous research investigating the impact of POM on 3D-printed dysphagia-friendly foods, this study investigates the feasibility of developing such foods via 3D printing by varying the concentration of XG (0, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 g kg -1 ). items.title: Addressable Control of Hybrid Spin Qubit in Single-Atom Copper-Modified Fullerene.
items.summary: Developing high-dimensional solid-state quantum technologies requires overcoming the trade-off between spin dimensionality and quantum coherence. Hybrid spin architectures offer a promising solution to expand the quantum state space bottom-up by combining rapid electronic manipulation with robust nuclear phase memory. However, solid-state hybrid spin materials capable of simultaneously supporting both electron and nuclear spin manipulations remain exceedingly rare. items.title: HERACLES for fast and accurate likelihood-based reconstruction of massive lineages
items.summary: CRISPR-based lineage recording technologies can trace the ancestry of hundreds of thousands of cells, yet reconstructing accurate phylogenies at this scale remains computationally challenging. Likelihood-based methods employ explicit evolutionary models of CRISPR editing that improve tree accuracy but require computationally expensive searches over tree topologies, whereas greedy distance-based alternatives scale efficiently but their accuracy requires distances that faithfully represent the true phylogeny. items.summary: Reconfigurable nonlinear-processing units (RNPUs) are multi-terminal electronic devices that act as computational primitives, exploiting intrinsic nonlinear charge transport combined with electrostatic tunability. Silicon-based realizations provide a scalable and technologically relevant platform toward unconventional computing hardware, yet the physical origin of their room-temperature nonlinearity has remained unresolved. Here, we demonstrate room-temperature operation in both boron- and arsenic-doped silicon RNPUs and show, using temperature- and length-dependent measurements supported by TCAD simulations, that charge transport is governed by space-charge effects. We introduce a unified taxonomy that organizes persistent updates by component, execution locus, feedback, loop closure, timescale, and budget, and distinguishes recursive changes to evaluators or update machinery. items.title: How many labels can a biological oscillator carry? A quality-factor screen for proposed information carriers.
items.summary: How many distinguishable labels can a biological oscillator carry? Proposals invoking collective vibrational modes, endogenous electromagnetic fields, microtubule excitations and oscillatory phase codes are each debated on grounds particular to themselves, with no shared standard for comparison. We show that spectral distinguishability alone bounds the number of labels by the quality factor, M≤Q=2πντ coh . items.title: Integration and annotation of spatial multi-omic data with DIRAC.
items.summary: Spatial multi-omic technologies measure multiple molecular layers within intact tissues. Two central challenges are vertical integration, which combines different molecular modalities, and horizontal integration, which aligns cell types across studies. Here we show domain invariant representation through adaptive calibration (DIRAC), a geometric deep learning model that unifies these tasks in a generalized domain adaptation framework. DIRAC learns task-discriminative features that are insensitive to domain shifts caused by batch effects, omic modalities or study sites, enabling a shared embedding space and automated cell-type annotation through label transfer from reference datasets.…

items.title: When, Where, and How Experience Becomes Structure: Mechanisms for Recursive Self-Improvement in LLM Agents
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) studies how AI systems modify themselves and carry those changes into the generation of subsequent improvements. LLM agents can pursue this process by using interaction experience to revise Prompt, Memory, Skill, and Harness in some cases while keeping the task-execution model’s weights fixed. However, execution feedback does not directly specify which component should change, and a locally successful revision may not remain useful across tasks or subsequent improvement cycles. items.title: Hierarchical semantic fusion in hyperbolic space for next POI recommendation.
items.summary: Next Point-of-Interest (POI) recommendation aims to suggest POIs that users are likely to visit next based on their recent check-ins. Recent studies suggest that POI-POI transitions and user-POI interactions exhibit hierarchical patterns that can be modeled in hyperbolic space, whose exponential volume growth enables compact and expressive representations. items.title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models
items.summary: Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond their training sets. Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. Here, we systematically benchmark diverse mutational effect and drug-target affinity prediction models using deep mutational scanning datasets spanning 11 inhibitor conditions for the MET kinase domain. items.title: Hyperbolic Hierarchical 3D Scene Representations for Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graph Generation.
items.summary: Open-vocabulary 3D scene graph generation aims to predict 3D objects and their predicates beyond the annotated label space. Compared to closed-set 3D scene graph generation methods, the open-vocabulary approach is more general, practical, and less dependent on labor-intensive ground truth annotations. Existing open-vocabulary 3D scene graph generation methods rely on learning individual object and predicate features in the representation space while ignoring higher-level 3D scene representations, leading to overfitting and suboptimal performance. items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping how AI itself is developed.
